In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the response to ESA is influenced by many factors, including the dose of rh-EPO, the type of dialysis, and the presence of malnutrition, inflammation (including the type of inflammatory stimulus), iron deficiency and/or iron overload, and the presence or not of a concomitant disease.
the inflammatory state and malnutrition are the main causes of ESA resistance in hemodialysis, and that the combination of these 2 conditions is a strong predictor of poor clinical outcome.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inflammation, malnutrition, resistance to ESA, and the outcome of hemodialysis patient are closely linked.

the inflammatory state, malnutrition, or both could be a major cause of ESA resistance and that, in turn, the ESA resistance could represent a link between malnutrition-inflammation, anemia, and the poor prognosis of chronic kidney disease.
ESA resistance is a multifaceted phenomenon, with a number of causes and consequences.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the response to rh-EPO in chronic hemodialysis patients is multifactorial and is influenced by a number of variables that include inflammation, malnutrition, iron status, comorbidity, and dialysis adequacy.
the definition of rh-Epo resistance has been introduced and that the relationship between dialyses, increased inflammatory stimulus and malnutrition and ESA response has been investigated.
